tasks.task: Write a one-page decision brief

items.when: Before the brief, to see if the choice can be undone and how much evidence is enough
When a leader must choose and needs the question, real options, costs, risks and a recommendation
When the options on the table look alike, to get two differently shaped plans with money and dates
When the room agrees too fast, to hear three thinkers argue the decision
When the choice is about money, to get cash impact, a downside case and numbers to check first
When the brief hides what is unknown, to set conditions for going on or stopping
When the brief is drafted, to have a fresh reviewer read it as the leader who must decide

tasks.task: Build the board pack

items.when: When the period's numbers and notes are in and the board meets this month
When the board must decide something, to get an evidence map and the update around it
When the pack reads as a list, to try another order for the story, the numbers and the bad news
When the pack is drafted, to get the toughest questions and drills on the weak numbers
Before it is sent, to give every figure and claim a dated source, a rewrite or a cut
When bad news is buried, to name the problem plainly and who owns the next step

tasks.task: Write the regular investor update

items.when: When investors expect the monthly or quarterly note and past updates set the format
When you want a second framing of the story, plus the questions investors will ask
When the period had a setback, to state the loss, the numbers and the next step briefly
When staff, board and investors hear different things, to find the contradictions
Before sending, to tie each number to the books or the source it came from

tasks.task: Write the monthly business report

items.when: Monthly, after the books close, with the board pack added when the board meets
When the same numbers are pulled each month and the report should rerun from a saved set-up
When actuals miss the budget, to say what moved, why, and give a short note for leaders
When the report is long, to put the answer, the impact in numbers and the decision on one page
When the report shows totals that always go up, to find numbers that show cause
Before numbers leave the workbook, to catch formula errors and broken links

tasks.task: Set a quarterly OKR set for a team or company

items.when: When there is a year plan and last period's numbers and you need a short OKR set with owners
When you want a second draft of objectives with dated key results to compare
When the team has no agreed main measure, to pick one and the few numbers that feed it
When key results count activity, to swap them for numbers that show a result
When goals list tasks, to ask what result the customer would notice

tasks.task: Review draft goals and fix them

items.when: When a team shares draft OKRs and you must check baseline, target, owner and data source
When the draft needs rewriting, with a scoring rule and a mid-quarter check routine
When two versions of the set exist and you want a fresh reviewer to pick one

tasks.task: Run check-ins and the quarter-end review

items.when: When the quarter is running and you need the check-in script, scorecard and confidence calls
At quarter end, to compare plan and results and say what to keep, cut or change
When managers must carry the goals into one-on-ones and settle disputes

tasks.task: Cut ten priorities to three

items.when: When the list of top priorities is long and the team must pick a few and park the rest
When cutting needs someone to say what stops, and who tells whom
When the business has no clear focus to rank against
When nobody will drop anything, to face the facts and choose what to stop

tasks.task: Write a strategy memo for one question

items.when: When a leader must think through one question, such as a new market or a pricing change
When evidence is in hand and the memo must set out choices, risks and missing facts
When the memo leans one way from the start, to set two different plans side by side
When the leadership team reads in silence and wants the full argument in sentences
When the memo is drafted, to score it and get the three fixes that matter
When the memo hides behind vague labels, to cut padding and say the plain thing

tasks.task: Run a pre-mortem on a big plan

items.when: Before a launch, senior hire, new site or price change that is hard to undo
When you want a second pass that imagines the plan failed a year on
When the bet is large, to see what the worst case costs and if the business survives it
When money is about to be committed, to get the strongest case against the plan
When the plan sounds certain, to turn it upside down and check incentives

tasks.task: Design or repair the operating rhythm

items.when: When meetings sprawl or decisions stall and each meeting needs an owner, pre-read and agenda
When you want another rhythm to compare, with metric reviews and decision rules by stage
When a meeting is in doubt, to cost it and decide whether to hold it at all

tasks.task: Prepare and follow up the weekly leadership meeting

items.when: Every week, to prepare the day before the meeting and follow up the same day
When the meeting needs an agenda and a pre-read drawn from existing pages
When one meeting must run from pre-read to notes with owners and dates
Each week, to check last week's open actions and set the next agenda
When the leader takes rough notes in calls and wants fuller notes with no bot present

tasks.task: Turn meeting notes into minutes and an action list

items.when: When you have rough notes and need decisions, actions with owners and dates, and open questions
When the meeting was a board or committee and minutes must follow a proper format
When actions sit across notes and emails, to get one list with owners, dates and sources

tasks.task: Write the cross-team project status

items.when: Before the leadership meeting, to turn team notes into one page of on track and blocked
When one project needs its own report with status, risks and decisions needed
When a cross-team project has no charter, owners or dependency list to report against

tasks.task: Draft a message in the leader's name

items.when: When an all-team note, investor reply or partner note must go out as the leader
When the same news goes to two audiences, to see it pitched each way
When the note needs manager talking points, a FAQ and a rollout order
When the message is a change of direction and needs a memo, a script and listening talks
Before it goes out, to have a fresh reviewer read it as the person receiving it

tasks.task: Run quarterly planning and review

items.when: In the last weeks of each quarter, to review, plan and set the next goals in order
When last quarter's plan and results are in, to see what to keep, cut or change
When requests outrun capacity, to balance build, improve and maintain with a not-doing list
When the plan adds work and removes none, to ask what to stop

tasks.task: Write the annual plan and the annual letter

items.when: When the annual plan must fit the yearly cycle of reviews and planning dates
When next year could go two ways, to compare two plans with money and dates
When the leader writes to the team or owners with principles and the year's honest numbers
Before the letter goes out, to tie every figure to the books

tasks.task: Prepare the leader for a board or investor meeting

items.when: Before the meeting, to drill the toughest questions and own the weak spots
When the leader needs a one-page brief of a long paper before walking in
When the leader will present, to reorder the talk so the stakes land early

tasks.task: Turn a report into a briefing deck

items.when: Before the slides, to try an outline that builds belief and ends in a clear ask
When a written report must become editable slides with text checked against the source
When a first draft of the deck is needed fast from an outline
Before the deck is shown, to check each slide's numbers against the report

tasks.task: Audit the leader's time and what to hand off

items.when: When last week's calendar is to hand, to count what was chosen and what was taken
When the founder does too much, to find what only they should do and a delegation plan
When incoming work needs a route and an owner, or the calendar needs keep or drop calls
When commitments pile up, to track changed promises and draft the follow-ups due

tasks.task: Keep the decision log and review past decisions

items.when: When a decision is made and must be logged with owner, date, reasons and a review date
When a past decision's result is known, to review the process and sharpen the checklist
When a decision went badly, to judge it by the process and not the result

tasks.task: Map who decides what and who must be consulted

items.when: When roles overlap, to get an org plan, a spans check and a chart of who decides what
When a project touches many people, to map power and interest and how to talk to each
When views clash, to weigh each by track record on the topic and reach a call

tasks.task: Plan a leadership offsite

items.when: When the team will meet off site and needs a decision-first agenda and a pre-read request
Before booking, to cost the days and check the offsite is worth holding
After the offsite, to turn the notes into one action list with owners and dates

always.when: Before anything goes to the board, investors or all staff, to catch typos and mixed terms
When a draft states a number or a market fact you cannot trace to company records

helpers.when: When the report needs a forecast, a budget or a variance analysis built from the books
When the board pack or all-hands deck must be designed, not only outlined
When a change needs a full staff communication plan across channels
When a cross-team project needs a plan, owners and tracking, not only a status page
When investor updates turn into a raise and need a deck, a model and a target list
When the work is the leader's inbox, calendar, travel and meeting logistics

gaps: No library item drafts in one named leader's voice from their past messages; only the kit prompt does
No library item assembles a full board pack with agenda, resolutions, committee papers and a pre-read schedule
No library item writes a company annual plan that ties goals to budget and headcount; only the annual letter is covered
No library item runs a weekly OKR check-in with confidence scores and a scorecard; only the kit skill does
No library item maps cross-team dependencies to show which team blocks which
No library item sets decision rights for a whole company; the one that exists covers product questions only
No library item prepares the monthly business review pack and its fixed agenda
No library item writes a leader's briefing note for an outside meeting from plain notes without a paid data tool
No library item makes three clearly different versions of a board update or leader message to compare
No library item keeps a dated decision register and brings each decision back on its review date
